turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would not be comforted by her words, that he was consumed by worry for her and for the future.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that his son must be married and settled before she could rest, that she would not die with her work undone

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung insisted that the time for marrying off their son was not now, but after his mother had recovered and was well.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that he was not thinking of her health, but of his own desires, and that he must think of her and their son's future.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son reassured his mother that he would not let her down, that he would marry the girl she liked and settle down as soon as possible.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told O-lan that she had prepared a simple meal for the family, hoping to lift everyone's spirits.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan looked at Wang Lung with a determined gaze and told him that he must let their son settle down as soon as possible, that her dying would bring peace to his son and his family

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she was exhausting herself with her worrying and that he would not let their son settle down as long as she had not fully recovered.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that his worrying was pointless, and that she must see their son married before she could find peace

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told Wang Lung that perhaps it would be better if he went out to the fields with the eldest son, as it would take their minds off their mother's illness.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan must not exhaust herself with such talk, that he would not have her worrying about their son's marriage until she was well again

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that his refusal to let their son settle down was cruel, and that he was only thinking of himself and not of their family's future

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother that he was willing to wait, and that as long as she was well, it did not matter when he married the maid.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung why he could not see the importance of their son's marriage, and why he continued to put it off

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid whispered to Wang Lung that it was indeed a good idea to distract himself with work, as his mother's illness weighed heavily on him.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would not have their son settle down with a woman until she was well and had given her blessing, for he would not have their son bound to a life of sorrow and hardship without his mother's guidance and approval

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan's voice grew weak, but her determination remained unwavering as she told Wang Lung that she understood his concerns, but she would not rest until their son was settled and happy, with a good wife to care for him.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she must not exhaust herself trying to settle their son's marriage, that she needed to rest and recover, and that he would take care of everything.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan looked at Wang Lung with a determined gaze and told him that she would not be convinced by his words, that she had seen too much suffering in her life to believe that their son's happiness depended on her own well-being.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan's health was the only thing that mattered to him, and that he would not rest until she was well and happy again

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing she had to attend to before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan should not speak of dying and that it would please him if she did not.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan replied that she had to die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wedded this good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served O-lan, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe O-lan's face when she sweated in pain. Now O-lan wanted her son to come home, because she had to die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she might die easily, knowing that her grandson was stirred into life and a great-grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they had said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan declared that she would see Wang Lung wedded and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan instructed Wang Lung to sit there and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked if everyone had wine, if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot, if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it, and if the eight fruits were present.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was now content and that this thing in her may do as it would. She instructed her son to look to his father and his grandfather, and her daughter to look to her husband and his father and his grandfather and the poor fool in the court, there she was. And she told Wang Lung that he had no duty to any other.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan said that, even if she was ugly, she had borne a son; although she was but a slave, there was a son in her house.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan insisted that no one else could feed Wang Lung's son and care for him as she did. She told Wang Lung that beauty would not bear a man sons.
